title: The Saratoga Club audition and number banker Cass Goldstein
summary: Russell assembled a band for the Saratoga Club across from the Savoy, owned by an indifferent number banker who promised pay whether or not customers came.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Then you came back to the Nest and replaced Simeon?
Oh yeah. I was in and out of work with the band like a swinging door. And any time I wanted to come back, 'Come on back.' If I ain't got nothin' to do, I come on back. Let me see, where we at now...?
Well, we're still at the Nest.
We're still at the Nest with Russell?>
Mmm-hmm.

Well, then he was getting his band together -- that's what it was. Because he thinks he has a job coming up, you know, or a band... A friend of his. A number banker. And that's when he tried to get all the men he could from...
Chicago?
Yeah, from Chicago. Albert Nicholas and
Holmes (10/9) - 86
all the rest of them.. But I don't think he got Nick right away. I think Nick went to China, or he went somewhere.

Anyway, Russell got his band together... I think this is when Higgenbotham come in... And we went to this place and made an audition, and the man was crazy about the band. Oh Lord, was he crazy about 'em. Cass Goldstein at the Saratoga Club. He was a big number banker. He said, "This is my place of business. If nobody comes in here, don't worry about it. You'll get paid just the same." Well, you know, ha-ha, "That sounds awful good, but how can you do it if nobody comes in." He says, "Let me worry about that." Well, I don't know nothin' about the man. I don't know he's a number banker. In fact, I didn't know what a number banker was.

And he had that place for his own amusement. I don't know, somebody laid that nightclub on him. He really didn't know what to do with it. He didn't care if nobody ever come in. He didn't care about nothin'. And the waiters, they were running the place, they were taking away all the money. All Goldstein was doing was paying for the whiskey and stuff. He was paying for everything. He didn't care. He didn't care a bit. And if Russell had been a real smart man, Russell could have got rich off of him just by knowing him. The man was good-hearted, you know.
Holmes (10/9) - 87

Of course, what can I say? I'm nothing but a kid. And of course, I never had no... I was never too aggressive anyway, no kind of way. But I never thought nothin' of trying to take anybody for anything. But I mean, the man's got it right there. All you've got to do is ask for it.
Now, where was the Saratoga Club located?

Right exactly across the street from the Savoy Ballroom. Not exactly. Well, there was only one other corner at the Savoy Ballroom, but it was on the other side, the opposite side of the street. The Savoy, I think, ran from One Hundred Fortieth Street to One Hundred Forty-First...
Yeah, the Savoy was on One Hundred Fortieth.
To One Hundred Forty First, right?
Yeah.
Well, this club was...
Right across.
...between Thirty-Ninth and Fortieth, on the opposite side of the street.
